slides.text:
`Println` prints values as they are. To place values inside a sentence, Go uses `Printf` with **verbs**: placeholders that start with `%`. Here you use the three you will meet every day, and `Sprintf`, which builds the text without printing it. All the verbs come later, in Strings and text.

The snippet is pseudo code, not Go.
slides.code:
template  "<name> is <age> years old"
values    "Ana", 30
result    Ana is 30 years old

exercises.title: Fill in a sentence
exercises.guide: Print a sentence with a name and an age inside it.

chunks.guide: The skeleton is already in the file. Start with the name.
And a whole number for the age.
`Printf` fills each `%` verb with the next value. `%s` is for text and `%d` for whole numbers.

notes.text: Printf adds no new line, so you add one.

chunks.text: fmt.Printf("%s is %d years old\n", name, age)

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick the output.
exercises.code:
package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
    name := "Go"
    fmt.Printf("Hello, %s!", name)
    fmt.Println("Bye")
}
exercises.explanation: `Printf` adds no new line, so `Bye` follows on the same line. `%s` is replaced by `Go`.

exercises.title: One verb for any value
exercises.guide: `%v` prints any value. Use it for a number and a bool.

chunks.guide: `%v` prints a value in its default form, whatever its type. It is the verb to use when you just want to see a value.

notes.text: The same verb works for a number and a bool.

exercises.title: The verb for text
exercises.guide: `%d` is for whole numbers. Use the verb that prints a string.

exercises.title: Build the text first
exercises.guide: `Sprintf` builds the text and returns it, so you can use it later.

chunks.guide: `Sprintf` works like `Printf`, but it returns the text instead of printing it.

notes.text: Returns the text instead of printing it.

exercises.title: Why does it not compile?
exercises.guide: Read the message, then pick the cause.
exercises.code:
./main.go:6:17: more than one character
  in rune literal
options: Text needs double quotes, not single quotes
exercises.explanation: Single quotes make one character, not text. Text goes between double quotes.
